reply:
No. The salt defeats rainbow tables, but leaves you exposed to brute force, which is the real threat after a breach.

MD5 does ~3 billion hashes/second on a GPU. bcrypt at cost=12 does ~60,000/second—about 50,000× slower. That speed gap matters concretely:

- A weak password (8 characters, common patterns) cracks on salted MD5 in hours or days on commodity hardware.
- The same password on bcrypt takes years per-user.

If your database leaks—and databases do leak—every user with a weak password gets their account compromised. Most passwords are weak. The pentester flagged this because the vulnerability is real and post-breach exploitation is trivial.

The salt only stops precomputation. It does not slow brute force. That requires an intentionally slow function.

Cost of being wrong: User account takeovers within days of a breach, not years.
